# @circle-fin/provider-gateway-v1

## 1.6.0

### Minor Changes

- Unified Balance Kit now supports EURC and cirBTC alongside USDC.

  - Pass `token: 'EURC'` or `token: 'cirBTC'` to any method that takes a token: `deposit`, `depositFor`, `estimateDeposit`, `spend`, `estimateSpend`, `getBalances`, `addDelegate`, `removeDelegate`, `getDelegateStatus`, `initiateRemoveFund`, and `removeFund`. Token names are case-insensitive, and leaving out `token` still means USDC.
  - EURC is available on Ethereum, Base, Avalanche, World Chain, Arc, and Solana, and on Ethereum Sepolia, Base Sepolia, Avalanche Fuji, Arc Testnet, and Solana Devnet. cirBTC is available on Ethereum and Arc, and on Ethereum Sepolia and Arc Testnet. Call `getSupportedChains(token)` to get the list at runtime.
  - Amounts are still decimal strings, such as `'0.0005'`. cirBTC accepts up to 8 decimal places and EURC up to 6. Amounts with more decimal places fail validation.
  - Fees are reported in the token being moved, and `spend()` results now include a `token` field.
  - Delegates are approved per token. A delegate you added for USDC must be added again with `token: 'EURC'` or `token: 'cirBTC'` before it can spend that token.
  - Forwarded spends (`useForwarder: true`) work with all three tokens. FAST deposits remain USDC-only; a FAST deposit with EURC or cirBTC fails with `INPUT_UNSUPPORTED_ROUTE` before any transaction is sent.

  TypeScript: `SupportedToken` (exported from App Kit as `UnifiedBalanceSupportedToken`) is now `'USDC' | 'cirBTC' | 'EURC'`. Exhaustive `switch` statements on it need cases for the new tokens.

### Patch Changes

- EURC address updates in chain definitions.

  - `WorldChain.eurcAddress` is now set; it was previously `null`.
  - The EURC addresses on Avalanche, Avalanche Fuji, and Base now use EIP-55 checksum casing instead of all lowercase. If you compare these addresses with `===`, compare them case-insensitively instead.
  - EURC can now be looked up by symbol on Avalanche Fuji and Solana Devnet.

- Spend fixes for Solana recipients and fee reporting. The amounts charged on-chain were already correct; these changes affect only errors and reported fees.

  - Spending to a Solana recipient that has no token account for the spent token (USDC or EURC) now fails before anything is signed, with an `INPUT_VALIDATION_FAILED` error. Previously the transfer reverted on-chain at mint time. The error message names each missing account, and `error.cause.trace.missingTokenAccounts` lists them. The SDK does not create token accounts: create the missing accounts, then call `spend()` again.
  - `estimateSpend()` runs the same check and throws the same error instead of returning fees.
  - If the account is missing only when the mint is submitted, the error is `RESUMABLE`. Create the account, then retry with `config.retry` using the attestation and signature in `error.cause.trace`.
  - Fees returned by `spend()` now show what was actually charged instead of the maximum allowed fee, so they can be lower than the fees from `estimateSpend()`. If the charged amounts are unavailable, `spend()` reports the estimated fees.
  - Fees returned for forwarded spends (`useForwarder: true`) no longer count the forwarding fee twice.

## 1.5.3

### Patch Changes

- Arc Testnet calls no longer fail with `HTTP request failed` when no custom RPC is configured. The default Arc Testnet RPC endpoint is now `https://rpc.testnet.arc.io`, replacing the retired `https://rpc.testnet.arc.network/` host. Apps that already pass their own Arc Testnet RPC URL or transport are unaffected.

## 1.5.2

### Patch Changes

- More EVM contract reverts now include a readable reason instead of a raw
  error selector. The SDK now also looks for the selector in the error's cause
  chain, in browser wallet errors, and in viem's raw revert data.

## 1.5.1

### Patch Changes

- Stop replacing a validation error with a `TypeError` when the rejected value
  holds a `bigint`.

  Building a validation error serializes the offending value into the message.
  `JSON.stringify` refuses `bigint` and circular structures, so a value that
  carried either — an on-chain read, or a transaction receipt log, both of which
  routinely hold `bigint` fields — threw
  `TypeError: Do not know how to serialize a BigInt` from inside the error
  constructor. The real error never surfaced, and callers saw an unrelated crash
  in its place.

  Such values now render with their `bigint` fields as strings, and a value that
  still cannot be serialized renders as `[unserializable object]`. The error's
  `cause.trace.value` is unchanged and still carries the raw value.

## 1.5.0

### Minor Changes

- Add Arc mainnet (`Blockchain.Arc`, chainId 5042) as a supported chain. Arc is wired for CCTP v2 bridging (`BridgeChain.Arc`, domain 26) with Circle's Forwarding Service enabled for Arc as a destination, and for Gateway v1 (`UnifiedBalanceChain.Arc`).
- Enable Circle's Forwarding Service as a destination for Arc mainnet. The Forwarding Service now supports Gateway transaction types on Arc, so a Gateway `spend` with `useForwarder: true` to an Arc mainnet destination is now accepted instead of being rejected up front.

## 1.4.0

### Minor Changes

- Add fast cross-chain deposit routing and forwarding support.

### Patch Changes

- Fix `getSupportedChains({ sourceFeeSupported: true })` over-reporting source-fee
  bridging support. Previously, source-fee eligibility was inferred from a contract
  address shared with the fast-deposit forwarding path, causing fast-deposit-only chains
  to appear supported and fail at the Quote API instead of being rejected client-side.
  Source-fee support is now gated on an explicit allowlist of eligible source chains.

## 1.3.0

### Minor Changes

- Configure custom HTTP headers for Circle Gateway API requests through
  `GatewayV1Config` and `UnifiedBalanceKitConfig`. AppKit's existing top-level
  `headers` option now also applies to Unified Balance Gateway requests, while
  `unifiedBalance.headers` can override it.

  The headers are sent with every Gateway API request the provider makes —
  balances, deposits, spend estimate, transfer, forwarder status polling, and
  `/v1/info` — and are merged on top of the SDK defaults (such as
  `Content-Type`) rather than replacing them.

### Patch Changes

- Fix `unifiedBalance.spend()` signing burn intents with the wrong wallet when
  multiple spend sources hold balance on the same chain.

  Each burn intent is now matched to and signed by its source wallet. A single
  developer-controlled adapter can also be reused for multiple wallet addresses,
  while exact duplicate spend sources remain rejected before signing.

## 1.2.1

### Patch Changes

- Read-only calls (Earn allowance checks, Gateway delegate and withdrawal-state
  lookups) no longer pass through `prepareAction`. If you wrap `prepareAction` to
  verify transactions before signing, these reads no longer appear there — only
  operations that may be signed or broadcast do.

## 1.2.0

### Minor Changes

- Support spending a unified balance from a smart contract account via Gateway's
  ERC-1271 programmable authorization.

  Previously, `spend` rejected any smart contract account (SCA) signer up front
  and told you to register an EOA delegate against the SCA, because Gateway
  validated burn-intent signatures with `ecrecover` only. Gateway now also
  validates contract signatures with ERC-1271, so the SDK detects a contract
  signer from its on-chain bytecode and marks the transfer request
  `contractSigner: true` — multisigs, passkey wallets, Circle SCA wallets, and
  other ERC-1271 accounts can authorize transfers directly.

  No API change: `spend` takes the same parameters and picks the validation path
  for you. EOA transfers are unaffected, and EIP-7702-delegated EOAs keep using
  the `ecrecover` path since their signatures verify that way.

  ERC-1271 validation is EVM-only. Solana burn intents are unchanged.

## 1.1.4

### Patch Changes

- Make the SDK safe to bundle and run in browsers/client-side apps.

  - Browser requests omit Node-only headers that would cause CORS failures, including EarnKit’s SDK-version header.
  - Solana operations in App Kit, Adapter Solana Kit, and Gateway work in a browser without requiring a consumer-provided `Buffer` polyfill.
  - Supplying a `kitKey` or Circle Wallets `apiKey` in a browser now fails early. Keep those secrets on the server and forward a prepared transaction or other safe result to the client.

## 1.1.3

### Patch Changes

- Fix automatic allocation (`amountIn`) sometimes failing with an insufficient-balance error even when your balance was sufficient.

  When you let the SDK choose which chains to draw from (passing `amountIn` instead of explicit `allocations`), a transfer could be rejected with `BALANCE_INSUFFICIENT_TOKEN` (9001) even though you held enough USDC, and topping up did not help.

  Auto-allocation now accounts for the network's actual gas fee before submitting, so these transfers go through. If your balance genuinely cannot cover the amount plus gas, you now get a clear `BALANCE_INSUFFICIENT_GAS` (9002) error naming the affected chain and the shortfall, instead of an opaque rejection — reduce the amount or add USDC on that chain. Transfers with explicit `allocations` are unchanged, and there is no extra latency unless a correction is actually needed.

## 1.1.2

### Patch Changes

- Fix a missing runtime dependency (`@coral-xyz/anchor` and `bn.js`) that could
  cause `Could not find package` errors under strict module resolvers (Deno,
  Supabase Edge Runtime, pnpm) when this package is installed directly.

## 1.1.1

### Patch Changes

- Internal dependency updates. No user-facing changes.

## 1.1.0

### Minor Changes

- Enable Circle's Forwarding Service as a destination for Solana (mainnet and devnet). A Gateway `spend` with `useForwarder: true` to a Solana destination is now accepted instead of being rejected.

### Patch Changes

- Error traces from BridgeKit, SwapKit, and UnifiedBalanceKit now carry the
  most recent on-chain transaction hash known to the failing operation,
  when one is available. BridgeKit walks the result steps (including
  pending broadcasts whose receipt has not yet landed). SwapKit and
  UnifiedBalanceKit capture the broadcast hash through a new internal
  `onBroadcast` callback threaded into the swap operation and into the
  gateway provider's `spend()` (as a new optional `options` argument with
  a `SpendOptions.onBroadcast` field).

## 1.0.6

### Patch Changes

- `deposit`, `depositFor`, `addDelegate`, `removeDelegate`, `initiateRemoveFund`, and `removeFund` no longer reject Gas Station-enabled smart-contract accounts (SCAs) with zero native balance. EOA wallets without native funds will still fail at simulation with the underlying RPC error.

## 1.0.5

### Patch Changes

- Internal dependency updates. No user-facing changes.

## 1.0.4

### Patch Changes

- Improves the error you get when attempting a Gateway spend with a smart-contract account (SCA) as the signer. The failure previously surfaced as a confusing `invalid integer value <nil>/<nil> for type uint256` response from the Circle Wallets backend; you now get a clear `INPUT_UNSUPPORTED_ACTION` error up front that points at the delegate workflow (`kit.unifiedBalance.addDelegate` + `kit.unifiedBalance.spend` with the delegate EOA as `from.address` and the SCA as `from.sourceAccount`).
- Fix `unifiedBalance.spend` auto-allocation to query the Gateway balance of `from.sourceAccount` (the delegated owner) instead of `from.address` (the signer) when both are provided. Previously, delegate-flow spends from a signer with zero Gateway balance threw `BALANCE_INSUFFICIENT_TOKEN` before reaching the Gateway API, even when the source account had sufficient funds.

## 1.0.3

### Patch Changes

- Internal dependency updates. No user-facing changes.

## 1.0.2

### Patch Changes

- Internal dependency updates. No user-facing changes.

## 1.0.1

### Patch Changes

## 1.0.0

### Major Changes

- Provider that powers the Unified Balance Kit, enabling instant cross-chain USDC transfers through Circle Gateway. Install alongside `@circle-fin/unified-balance-kit` or use standalone for lower-level control.
